name: Sunfish Pond Appalachian Trail Free Primitive Campsite

management_agency.name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJ DEP) / ATC

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fee or permit required for primitive trail camping along AT corridor
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 1 night stay limit for long-distance / section hikers along AT
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Primitive camping permitted only at designated AT campsites/shelters along Kittatinny Ridge. Camping directly on Sunfish Pond shores strictly prohibited to protect glacial tarn ecology.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Use on-site privy where available; otherwise dig cat-hole 6-8 inches deep in rocky soil, at least 200 feet from Sunfish Pond and streams. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out. Black bears active: food storage bear hang or canister mandatory.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish completely cold before departing.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey New Jersey Forest Fire Service burn bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved interstate highway parking (I-80 Dunnfield Creek lot) followed by 3.5 mile walk-in trail
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Paved interstate highway access to trailhead parking lot. Campsite itself is walk-in / hike-in.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (parked at Dunnfield Creek lot)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 3-4 bars 5G/LTE (20-45 Mbps download on Kittatinny Ridge)
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (High ridge elevation overlooking Delaware Water Gap corridor)

amenities: Glacial Tarn Lake Scenery (Sunfish Pond - National Natural Landmark)

nearest_supply_towns.town_name: Delaware Water Gap, PA / Columbia, NJ

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 50-65°F, blooming mountain laurel, crisp ridge breezes.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 75-85°F, shaded hardwood canopy, popular hiking season.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Spectacular Delaware Water Gap autumn leaf foliage (50-65°F daytime, 35-45°F nights), dry trail conditions.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cold 20-35°F, snow-covered ridge trail, freezing nights.

dangers_and_hazards: Black Bears active along Kittatinny Ridge - bear hang or canister mandatory
Copperheads and Timber Rattlesnakes active near rocky outcrops

common_human_made_sounds: Distant Interstate 80 traffic hum down in Delaware Water Gap gorge

human_demographics_and_culture: Appalachian Trail thru-hikers, section backpackers, digital nomads, and Delaware Water Gap nature lovers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Lenape (Delaware) indigenous traditions revere the Kittatinny Ridge and Sunfish Pond ('Minisink') as sacred ancestral highlands where sky and spirit meet.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Glacial tarn lake energy, high ridge atmospheric ionization, fast 5G connectivity.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Appalachian Trail - Dunnfield Creek to Sunfish Pond
